_doc: The single-station test sites of rpp.ibr (Christian, 10 Nov 2026: 'We'll use these three as the test sites ... the single sites should come from a config file'). python -m rpp single-sites [LABEL ...] runs them: the dense step in the block, then mesh / depthmaps --photometry / ods into <out>/<label>/ (rover masked out) and <out>/<label>/with_rover/ (rover shown). Per station: 'site' (a site of rpp/data/sites.json; the block is its Navcam WORK folder) or 'work' (a block folder), 'station' (S003D2046 / 3_2046), 'frames' (the dense step's frames: 'images' [names], 'scale' (0.5: the half-resolution frames), 'sequences' [NCAM...]); optional 'variants' (rover, masked; the rover shown is the default since 0.96.1, run first), 'ods_exclude' (frames left out of the panorama, both eyes of a pair: an NLF stem drops its NRF partner), 'mesh_args' / 'depthmaps_args' / 'ods_args' (extra arguments), 'note'. Top level: 'dense_args' / 'mesh_args' / 'depthmaps_args' / 'ods_args' for every station (and per station the same keys); 'ods_args' --bits 16: the panorama from 16-bit linear frames. 0.97.0 (Christian, 12 Nov 2026): run by run_single_site_ibr.bat; 'ods_args' --eyes left right centre adds the panorama from the pivot (<station>[_rover]_ods_centre.png, _centre_16.png) and its depth (_centre_depth.npz, _depth_16.png, _depth_linear.jpg, _depth_log.jpg); the driver gives both variants of a station one <out>/<label>/tone_levels.json so their 16-to-8-bit scaling is the same; the pivot is on the azimuth axis at the Mastcam-Z height (--pivot-height zcam, the default) whatever cameras are rendered. 0.97.7 (Christian, 13 Nov 2026): per station 'name', the site's name in the mark at the panorama's nadir (default: from 'site'); 'ods_args' --fill-cameras F: the station's front Hazcam pair colours the terrain the Navcam frames do not see (under the arm). 0.97.8: 'depthmaps_args' --add-cameras F: the front Hazcam pair also gets its depth and photometric maps. 0.97.11: the centre panorama is no longer rendered (it took a third of the time; --eyes left right centre in 'ods_args' brings it back); the depth from the pivot is still made, from rays alone. 0.97.14 (Christian, 13 Nov 2026): the stations' labels carry the sol of their frames, Sol0052_S003D2046 - the folder <out>/<label>/ and the files' prefix; the dense workspace in the block stays dense_S003D2046, and the old label still selects the station on the command line. 0.97.14: the per-image maps (depthmaps) are made for the terrain-only variant alone ('depthmaps_variants': ["masked"]; ["rover", "masked"] for both) and hold depth and normals; 'photometry': true (top level or per station) adds incidence, emission, phase and shadow. 0.97.15 (Christian, 13 Nov 2026): per station 'context' [names]: frames of the block from another place, or from this place on another sol - added to the dense step's frames (terrain) and given to rpp ods --context-images (fill-only sources, their rover mask applied in both variants, never on the rover model); 0.97.19: with any way of choosing the station's frames (rpp dense --add-images). 0.97.17 (Christian, 13 Nov 2026: 'the name of the ods should just be its block name without any large, huge, or tiny additions'): the name in the mark and in the viewer's title is the block's label in sites.json without its size word (van_zyl_overlook_huge: Van Zyl Overlook; witch_hazel_large: Witch Hazel Hill); the stations carry no 'name' any more ('name' still overrides). 0.98.14: 'terrain': 'block' (a station, or top level for all): the dense step runs on every Navcam frame of the block (rpp dense --whole-block; the workspace colmap/dense_block_N is shared by the block's stations) and the mesh is made from that cloud; the panorama and the per-image maps still use the station's own 'frames'. 0.98.19 (Christian, 16 Nov 2026): 'terrain': 'block:<name>' - the block's cloud from the frames of 'terrain_sets'.<name>.images only (rpp dense --whole-block --block-name <name> --block-images ...; workspace colmap/dense_block_<name>), shared by the stations naming it: rockytop (the half-resolution end-of-drive 360s and the quarter-resolution mid-drive pairs of sols 460-502) and hippo_pools (sols 1947-2022); 'terrain': 'block' is still every Navcam frame of the block. Their 'context' frames: the end-of-drive and mid-drive sets within 20 m taken within 45 minutes of the station's local time (else the two within 20 m closest in time).

Run only when named. 0.98.22 (Christian, 16 Nov 2026: "for the z34 ods, somehow the z34 frames are not projecting on to the rover very well"): ZCAM08692 and the sol 688 Navcam 360 are processed without the mask model here (the deck-fiducial work), so their rover was painted on the ground in the terrain-only panorama; frames whose mask leaves the rover in now take the rover model's silhouette (rpp.ibr.ods.model_rover_masks), and the station renders the rover variant too, where the Mastcam-Z frames colour the rover model. 0.98.25 (Christian, 16 Nov 2026: "the z34 without the rover still has a lot of hardware. you may need to rerun those images with the mask inference enabled"): the silhouette missed the rover's edges, so the panorama runs the mask model on every frame the block made without it (colmap/masks_ibr, rpp.ibr.rover_masks); the block's own masks and alignment are unchanged.
